examples.en: Put on a hat, it's cold outside.
Mom dressed the child.

related.en: to put on (oneself) — надеть пальто, to put on a coat
to dress (someone else) — одеть ребёнка, to dress a child

note: Even native speakers mix them up. Mnemonic: наде́ть оде́жду (put on clothes), оде́ть Наде́жду (dress Nadezhda).

examples.en: My grandma bakes delicious pirozhki.

examples.ru: Что эта [ба́ба] кричит на весь двор?
examples.en: What is that woman yelling about for the whole yard to hear?

related.en: woman — colloquial, often rude
grandmother, grandma — on the mother's or the father's side

note: On its own, «ба́ба» is a coarse word for a woman, not a short form of «ба́бушка». A grandmother is «ба́бушка».

examples.en: How do you spell this word?
The Russian alphabet has thirty-three letters.
The minister gave a short speech.

related.en: word — a unit of language: одно́ сло́во, но́вое сло́во
letter (of the alphabet) — a written sign: большая бу́ква, a capital letter
speech, talk — a speech or the way of speaking: речь президе́нта

examples.en: This is a really beautiful thing.
That's none of your business!

related.en: thing, item — a physical object; the plural ве́щи also means belongings
matter, business, case — abstract: не твоё де́ло, none of your business

examples.en: This is my wife, her name is Anna.
A woman with a bag is standing at the door.

related.en: wife — моя жена́, my wife
woman — an adult female in general: незнакомая же́нщина, a strange woman

note: жена́ means only «wife». For a woman in general, say же́нщина.

examples.en: I don't feel like cooking today.
My brother is very lazy.

related.en: laziness — a noun: мне лень, I can't be bothered
lazy — an adjective: лени́вый челове́к, a lazy person

note: «лень» is a noun, not an adjective: say «мне лень» (+ dat.) or «я лени́вый», never «я лень».

examples.en: We are for peace all over the world.
Please turn off the light.

related.en: peace; world — во всём ми́ре, all over the world
light — включи́ свет, turn on the light

note: «свет» can also mean «world», but only in set phrases like «на бе́лом све́те» (in this world).

examples.en: I like writing letters.
The little boy needs to pee.

related.en: to write — писа́ть письмо́, to write a letter
to pee — child talk and colloquial

note: Only the stress tells these verbs apart, so a wrong stress changes the meaning.

examples.en: My grandmother has a beautiful garden.
Wait, I'll be right there.
Now I understand everything.

related.en: garden, orchard — я́блоневый сад, an apple orchard
now, right now, in a moment — сейча́с приду́, I'll be right there
now (as opposed to before) — a change from an earlier state

note: «сейча́с» also means «in a moment»: «я сейча́с приду́» is «I'll be right there». For «now» as opposed to earlier, use «тепе́рь».

examples.en: She is wearing dark blue jeans.
The sky is light blue today.

related.en: dark blue, navy — си́нее мо́ре, the deep blue sea
light blue, sky blue — голубо́е не́бо, a light blue sky

note: Russian treats these as two separate colors, not as shades of one «blue».

skip: built on Serbian склад/слога; not a confusion for English speakers

examples.en: I'm studying the Slovenian language.
Russian is a Slavic language.

related.en: Slovenian — of Slovenia: слове́нский язы́к
Slavic — of the Slavs: славя́нские язы́ки

note: Slovaks are «слова́ки», Slovenes are «слове́нцы»: three different words, easy to mix up.

examples.en: Put the books on the table.
Sit down on the chair.
Moscow is the capital of Russia.

related.en: table — обе́денный стол, a dining table
chair — сесть на стул, to sit down on a chair
capital city — столи́ца страны́, the capital of a country

note: «стол» and «стул» sound alike: table and chair. «Столи́ца» comes from «стол» in its old sense of a throne and means only a capital city.

examples.en: Russia is a big country.
The house is on the other side of the street.
Open the book to page five.

related.en: country — иностра́нная страна́, a foreign country
side, direction — пра́вая сторона́, the right side
page (of a book) — страни́ца кни́ги, a page of a book

note: «сторона́» is also a side in a dispute: «он на мое́й стороне́» means «he is on my side».

examples.en: Keep the receipt in case you want to return the item.
Could you bring the check, please?

related.en: receipt — from a shop or a till; also a bank check
bill, check — in a restaurant; account — счёт в ба́нке, a bank account

skip: built on Serbian шина (rail) vs Russian ши́на (tire)

examples.en: An avocado costs one hundred rubles apiece.
The fisherman caught a big pike.

related.en: piece, item — три шту́ки, three pieces; colloquially also a thing
pike — a fish: лови́ть щу́ку, to catch a pike

note: Watch the spelling: «шту́ка» with ш, «щу́ка» with щ. Colloquially «шту́ка» also means "thing": «что э́то за шту́ка?»

examples.en: Raspberry is a tasty berry.
I bought a kilo of strawberries.
We picked wild strawberries in the forest.

related.en: berry — any berry: малина, смородина, черника
strawberry (garden) — the usual shop strawberry
wild strawberry — the small forest one

note: In everyday speech «клубни́ка» is the strawberry you buy; «земляни́ка» is the small wild one.

skip: built on Serbian позор (attention) vs Russian позо́р (disgrace)
built on Serbian позориште (theater) vs Russian позо́рище (disgrace)

examples.en: She has a red dress.
What a beautiful city!

related.en: red
beautiful, pretty

note: The two look alike, but «кра́сный» means only red. Very beautiful, wonderful is «прекра́сный».
